headline: 11-party alliance says public trust in govt has hit rock bottom
summary: The Jamaat-led alliance claims the government's first 180 days have been marked by mismanagement, fuel shortages, and a failure to implement public mandates.
details: The Jamaat-led 11-party alliance has stated that public trust in the government has reached its lowest point over the last six months. This assessment was shared by Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizen Party (NCP) and opposition chief whip, following a meeting at the leader of the opposition's residence in Dhaka.

The alliance criticized the government for failing to implement the public mandate of the referendum and refusing to take the oath for the Constitution Reform Council. They claimed that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's promises to stabilize the nation and economy have resulted in widespread mismanagement.

Nahid Islam highlighted severe load-shedding across the country, including the capital, and noted that hundreds of factories are shutting down due to fuel and gas shortages. He also mentioned a fertilizer crisis that is severely impacting farmers.

The opposition further criticized the government's foreign policy, specifically regarding India. They argued that the government failed to hold India accountable for allowing the Awami League to hold a press briefing in Delhi on August 5.

The alliance stated that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to India would not benefit the country until the Awami League issue is resolved and justice is ensured for Sheikh Hasina and the killers of Osman Hadi.

The 11-party alliance is now planning a series of long marches. The first is scheduled for September 5 from Dhaka to Chattogram, followed by Dhaka to Rangpur on September 19, and others towards Jashore and Sylhet in October and November.

headline: 4 family members killed in Rangpur city
summary: Police have arrested two suspects in connection with the murder of a retired teacher, his wife, daughter, and 12-year-old son.
details: Retired Rangpur Zilla School teacher Ganapati Chakraborty (65), his wife Pritilata (50), his daughter Agami (23), and his son Priyam (12) were found murdered in their home in the Daspara area of Rangpur city.

The bodies were recovered on Saturday night. The mother and daughter were found on the staircase, the father on the roof, and the son under a bed. Police reported that the faces of all four victims were burnt with chemicals.
Police arrested Mughdho Das (21) and Siddhartha Das (19), both residents of Daspara. The suspects allegedly entered the house through an adjacent building on Thursday night while using yaba.

According to the Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner, the suspects confessed to strangling the victims one by one. They allegedly stayed in the house after the murders, used more yaba and ate food from the refrigerator before looting valuables.
Some recovered gold ornaments were found in an abandoned building nearby. A murder case has been filed by the victims' elder brother, Gopinath Chakraborty.
However, the victims' relatives believe a larger gang may be involved in the planned killings. They have called for a proper investigation to reveal the full mystery.
The victims' family members had been unreachable by phone since Thursday night, and the bodies were only discovered after relatives arrived at the house on Saturday night.

Retired Rangpur Zilla School teacher Ganapati Chakraborty (65), his wife Pritilata (50), his daughter Agami (23), and his son Priyam (12) were found murdered in their home in the Daspara area of Rangpur city.

The bodies were recovered on Saturday night. The mother and daughter were found on the staircase, the father on the roof, and the son under a bed. Police reported that the faces of all four victims were burnt with chemicals.

Police arrested Mughdho Das (21) and Siddhartha Das (19), both residents of Daspara. The suspects allegedly entered the house through an adjacent building on Thursday night while using yaba.

According to the Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner, the suspects confessed to strangling the victims one by one. They allegedly stayed in the house after the murders, used more yaba and ate food from the refrigerator before looting valuables.

Some recovered gold ornaments were found in an abandoned building nearby. A murder case has been filed by the victims' elder brother, Gopinath Chakraborty.

However, the victims' relatives believe a larger gang may be involved in the planned killings. They have called for a proper investigation to reveal the full mystery.

The victims' family members had been unreachable by phone since Thursday night, and the bodies were only discovered after relatives arrived at the house on Saturday night.
